svg.text: Guidemen — the source model itself has the inverted roof
2026-09-18 • source audit of Guidemen_GuideGate_UE5_100M_Instanced.glb • the defect is in the source, not the import
The source, found and extracted
C:\Works\Raw3DModels\V5\
Guidemen_GuideGate_UE5_ModelPlusGenerated4KMaterials.zip
Model/Guidemen_GuideGate_UE5_100M_Instanced.glb — 74.8 MB
18,823 scene nodes · 48 geometry definitions · 8 materials
16,248 roof-tile instances · 8 full PBR material sets + 8 4K sheets
Y-up, metres: 56.39 W x 20.26 H x 18.00 D
Extracted to
Saved/RawModelImport/V5/GuidemenRebuild/source/
The ridge runs along X — confirmed three ways
All 12 `G_RidgeBeast` ornaments sit at Z = 0.0, spread along X
from −14.7 to +14.7. They sit on the ridge, so that IS the ridge line.
Both ridge bars run along X at Z ≈ 0. The building is 56 m wide in X and
18 m deep in Z, so X is where a ridge belongs. No mis-axed bar.
Shell families agree: Front/Back span 31 m in X (main slopes, sloping in Z),
Left/Right span 15.5 m in X (hip ends, sloping in X).
The shells are inverted IN THE SOURCE
Measured from the source vertices, at the inner edge (near the ridge) and
the outer edge:
R1_RoofShellLeft inner Y=14.708 outer Y=16.269
R1_RoofShellRight inner Y=14.708 outer Y=16.269
R2_RoofShellLeft inner Y=18.628 outer Y=19.966
R2_RoofShellRight inner Y=18.628 outer Y=19.966
Every hip shell is higher at its outer edge than at the ridge — a valley, in
the source file. The V5 import reproduced it faithfully.
Why this explains everything that went wrong
source tiles span Y 12.92 .. 18.64 ridge bar R1 Y 14.72..15.00 ornaments Y 15.18..15.58 → these agree
source shells R1 span Y 14.62 .. 16.34 i.e. 1.63 m ABOVE the tiled surface, and sloping the wrong way
The tiles, the ridge bars and the ridge ornaments all agree with each other. The eight shells do not. So the source has one coherent roof and a set of
shells sitting above it, inverted — which is exactly the valley the user has been seeing through every pass, and exactly what my UE-side measurements
kept contradicting themselves about, because I was measuring a surface that disagrees with the roof it sits on.
It also means the shell fix already applied (flip + reseat to 12.90..14.62, just under the tiles at 12.92..14.72) puts them exactly where the source's own
tile span says they belong — matching the tiles to within 2 cm on both tiers.
Rebuild plan — and the one decision it needs
1. Source is extracted and audited: Saved/RawModelImport/V5/GuidemenRebuild/source/ — GLB, 8 PBR material sets, 8 4K sheets, build report.
2. The existing V5 pipeline (Scripts/PrepareV5Buildings.py) already knows how to import this package and build the 47-component HISM Blueprint.
3. Rebuild into a NEW task-owned package so the current asset stays recoverable, then re-apply the reference tuning and the shell correction.
The decision: a clean rebuild from this source reproduces the shell defect.
So the rebuild must either correct the shells after import (flip + reseat, as already done and verified on the current asset), or the source GLB should be
corrected upstream and re-exported. Correcting it in the pipeline is reversible and keeps the source untouched; that is the recommendation.
What is now known for certain
• The ridge runs along X at Z = 0 — established from three independent parts of the source (ornaments, both ridge bars, shell families). No mis-axed ridge.
• The roof tiles, ridge bars and ornaments form one coherent, correct roof in the source: tiles top at Y 14.71 / 18.64, ridge bars 14.72–15.00 / 18.65–18.92.
• The eight roof shells are inverted in the source and sit 1.63 m above the tiled surface. That is the defect, and it is upstream of Unreal.
• The source's tile span (12.92–14.72 lower, 17.03–18.65 upper) is what the shell correction was matched against, to within 2 cm.
